description: An open-source music player and MilkDrop visualizer for low-power PortMaster handhelds, Raspberry Pi OS, Linux and Windows. Installation and runtime dependencies.
hero_description: Give your handheld a second life as a music player. Browse and play with the joystick, then watch your tracks, demoscene classics and internet radio bloom into MilkDrop visuals.
screenshot_alt: Actual GlitchScope interface with a tracker music library and a MilkDrop waveform visualization
features_title:
A little player.
A deep collection.
features_intro: From the FLACs on your SD card to the MODs you grew up with. Bring your own music and find something new along the way.

features.title: Music you can see.
features.text: MilkDrop-compatible visuals powered by projectM 4. Preview presets, switch with the shoulder buttons, or let them rotate while you listen.

features.title: Old-school. New favorites.
features.text: Play everyday audio, tracker modules and chip music. Explore Modland and ModArchive, then keep discoveries in three favorites playlists.

features.title: Tune in. Take it offline.
features.text: Find internet radio through Radio Browser. Local files and cached downloads stay playable offline; radio and new downloads need a connection.

hardware_description: Run it on Linux handhelds, single-board computers and desktops. Builds target 64-bit ARM and x86-64. Adaptive resolution and frame-rate limits help you balance the visuals with the hardware you have.
hardware_note: Joystick controls, D-pad navigation and shoulder-button shortcuts come first. To launch, the device still needs a supported CPU architecture, SDL2, graphics and audio drivers, and the runtime libraries listed below.
install_intro: Choose your platform for installation steps and the libraries it needs. Release files are on GitHub; source-build instructions are below if a suitable binary is unavailable.
copy_failed: Copy failed. Select and copy the command manually.

platforms.label: PortMaster
platforms.title: A new use for your handheld.
platforms.intro: Designed for joystick play on Linux handhelds that meet the ARM64 runtime requirements below. The launcher picks up your firmware's button mappings and audio setup.
steps: A PortMaster catalogue listing is planned. When it goes live, find GlitchScope in the PortMaster app and select Install.
Until then, download the PortMaster ZIP from GitHub Releases and use the autoinstall folder for your firmware. Open PortMaster to install it.
Add your tracks to glitchscope/music/ and launch GlitchScope from Ports. Press Start to open the menu.
platforms.requires: Compatible PortMaster firmware with glibc 2.36+, SDL2, OpenGL ES 2 (GLESv2), ALSA, and working graphics and audio drivers.
platforms.bundled: Native audio decoders, codec libraries, zlib, libstdc++ and libgcc. No demo music is included.
platforms.note: PortMaster handhelds use the controls mapped by your firmware. Check runtime-requirements.txt in the archive and your firmware's device guide for compatibility and the correct autoinstall location.

platforms.label: Raspberry Pi OS
platforms.title: Make a little listening station.
platforms.intro: Use the Linux ARM64 archive on 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm. The older 32-bit Raspbian system cannot run this ARM64 package.
steps: Install the system libraries shown here on 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm.
Extract the Linux ARM64 release archive and keep its libs.aarch64 folder beside the launcher.
Add tracks to the music folder and run ./run-glitchscope.sh from the extracted directory.
platforms.requires: 64-bit ARM Linux, glibc 2.36+, SDL2, OpenGL ES 2, ALSA, and working display/GPU and audio drivers. A graphical session is needed.
platforms.bundled: Audio decoders, codec libraries and the C++ runtime. The same ARM64 package also supports other Linux distributions with these libraries.
platforms.command:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install libsdl2-2.0-0 libgles2 libasound2
./run-glitchscope.sh
platforms.note: Commands target Debian 12 / Bookworm. On Debian 13 / Trixie, replace libasound2 with libasound2t64. Other distributions may use different package names.

platforms.label: Linux
platforms.title: The desktop gets a turn, too.
platforms.intro: Download the Linux AMD64 archive for an x86-64 desktop. Debian 12 Bookworm provides a compatible runtime. ARM64 users can follow the Raspberry Pi OS tab's Linux ARM64 instructions.
steps: Install the runtime libraries shown here. Docker and a Go toolchain are not needed to run a release.
Extract the Linux AMD64 archive. Place your tracks in the music folder beside the executable.
Run ./glitchscope from the extracted directory. Press Tab for the menu or Ctrl+F for borderless fullscreen.
platforms.requires: glibc 2.35+, a C++ runtime providing GLIBCXX_3.4.30, SDL2, desktop OpenGL, ALSA, Vorbis, mpg123 and zlib. Install a working GPU driver.
platforms.bundled: The application and native audio decoders. You do not need the ffmpeg command-line tool; AMD64 uses the system codec and C++ libraries listed below.
platforms.command:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install libsdl2-2.0-0 libgl1 \
  libvorbisfile3 libvorbis0a libmpg123-0 \
  zlib1g libstdc++6 libasound2
./glitchscope
platforms.note: On Debian 13 / Trixie, use libmpg123-0t64 and libasound2t64. The GLIBCXX_3.4.30 requirement matters even when your glibc is new enough.

platforms.label: Windows
platforms.title: Unzip. Add music. Press play.
platforms.intro: Use the Windows AMD64 ZIP on 64-bit Windows, with your keyboard, mouse or gamepad.
steps: Download the Windows AMD64 release ZIP and extract the entire archive.
Keep SDL2.dll and the other packaged files beside glitchscope.exe. Add tracks to the music folder.
Launch glitchscope.exe. Press Tab to open the menu; Ctrl+F toggles borderless fullscreen.
platforms.requires: 64-bit Windows and a graphics driver supporting desktop OpenGL. Graphics and audio system libraries come from Windows and the device drivers.
platforms.bundled: SDL2.dll and native audio decoders. No separate SDL2 or ffmpeg installation is required.
platforms.note: Install your GPU manufacturer's driver if OpenGL initialization fails. The published package targets AMD64; an Android APK is not provided.

compatibility_title: What counts as a compatible Linux device?
compatibility_text: GlitchScope runs on compatible Linux devices of every form factor: PortMaster-supported handhelds, other Linux handhelds, single-board computers and desktop PCs. Current builds target 64-bit ARM and x86-64; each device's firmware must provide the graphics and audio stack listed above. Check PortMaster's device list and your firmware's compatibility notes:
retroid_text: An Android handheld such as Retroid Pocket Mini needs compatible Linux firmware to run this Linux app. There is no native Android build. Check the device-specific firmware instructions before switching systems:
compatibility_footer: Verify the firmware's glibc version and SDL2, GLES/OpenGL and ALSA drivers before installing. A firmware version can differ between two devices with the same model name.
build_description: On a Linux build host, install Git with submodule support, Docker, Make, Python 3 and binutils. Docker builds the native dependencies. Allow internet access for the first build and asset downloads. Run the target for your platform:
controls_intro: The interface is designed for joystick play: navigate with the D-pad, reach for the shoulders to switch presets, and use the buttons for playback and menus. Keyboard, mouse and touch work too. The player footer shows the controls for each screen.
community_description: Made by dendec, built on projectM, SoLoud, FFmpeg and a whole scene of audio pioneers. Explore the code, report a bug, or help your favorite handheld find its rhythm.
footer_text: Music player + MilkDrop visualizer. Free software, for the love of it.
